html:
SMTO-GML-0046 — The Gmail sign-in app you named isn't set up correctly

GUID: e5206fc9-e508-4a45-ad5c-fc50a6457d59
Slug: gmail-oauth-app-invalid
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • The saved entry you named is either not a Gmail OAuth App or is missing details SMTO needs to start Google sign-in. SMTO stopped before contacting Google, so nothing in Gmail changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select More options › Parameter Store, open the entry with the name you used, and check it was made from the Gmail OAuth App template, not another kind of entry. Gmail setup only accepts a Gmail OAuth App entry; a server, password or Google Workspace app entry is rejected.
  2. In that entry, make sure the client ID is filled in and the client type is desktop or web. For a web app, also enter the redirect address you registered with Google. SMTO can't start the Google sign-in when any of these details are missing or wrong.
  3. Leave the sign-in addresses Google provides as they are, and don't add extra fields. Keep the client secret private. Changed addresses or unknown fields make the entry fail SMTO's checks.
  4. Ask SMTO in the conversation to connect Gmail again using that entry, for example 'Connect Gmail using @gmail_auth_app'. Once the entry is correct, connecting is safe to repeat.

What success looks like

  • The Google sign-in page opens and SMTO reports your Gmail account as connected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or your Google Cloud project. Don't paste the client secret into the conversation, and don't keep resubmitting the same entry unchanged.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • GmailParameterProfiles.resolve found the requested key, but its profile_type is not gmail_oauth_app or its fields fail the Gmail OAuth App template validation (gmail_oauth_app_invalid).

What this means

  • GmailParameterProfiles.resolve finds a different profile type or invalid typed fields for the selected gmail_oauth_app key. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • GmailParameterProfiles.resolve finds a different profile type or invalid typed fields for the selected gmail_oauth_app key.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect client type/ID, redirect URI and required private secret fields against the selected template.

How to fix it

  • Open the key in Parameter Store: profile_type must be gmail_oauth_app with service 'gmail', client_type 'desktop' or 'web', a non-empty client_id, at least one scope, https authorization_uri and token_uri, and for client_type 'web' an http(s) redirect_uri with a host; no extra fields are allowed. A google_oauth_app (Google Workspace OAuth App) record must be used with auth.google_connect instead of gmail.connect.
  • Correct the OAuth application type, client ID and required redirect URI in the parameter template. Keep its client secret private.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended app passes typed validation and uses its supported private configuration.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
